MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-2-1 GRAB AND PLAY

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Up to 10 players go to each basket. Coaches will act as the facilitators. Two offensive players will start in different spacings, with one player holding the ball. The moment they pass the ball to the coach, the live 2-on-2 commences with the player going to grab the ball while a defender chases to hi-five the facilitator. As soon as both teams play, the next two teams must be ready immediately to play. Players must organize their own rotations.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Give the defense a hi-five further away to increase the offensive advantage.
- The offensive player is allowed to cut backdoor as opposed to grabbing the ball. In this case, the facilitator must pass the ball. On a cut, the defender does not need to continue sprinting to the defender to hi-five, but must immediately recover.
- Utilize the weakside dunker on every repetition.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### STAFF ROLE

- Change the size of the advantage based on the personnel (hand closer to the defense = smaller advantage, hand further away = bigger advantage).

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Spacing to keep the advantage
- Making drive and kick decisions when the help defender is activated

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you find a window to space outside the perimeter, or cut towards the basket?

Load for younger players

MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-3 AROUND THE CONE

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 cone and 1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Begin with an offensive player holding a ball and under the basket, facing the 3PT line. A defender will stand behind them. Another offensive player and defender will stand in the right corner, with another offensive player and defender in the left corner. The offense can start at any moment by dribbling around the cone. The defender must trail, creating an advantage situation for a live 3-on-3.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Making drive and kick decisions when the help defender is activated
- Converting advantages
- Defense working to recover back to neutral

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Increase the offensive advantage by having the defense run behind a second cone placed behind the first cone.
- Change the location of the offensive teammate across each repetition, also utilizing the top and the dunker. Stay for three repetitions before changing roles.
- Players receive double points for a no-look pass assist.
- Add an extra cone, players can choose what side they dribble to. Other offensive players must start in bad spacing and find a good spacing location to re-space to as the dribble starts.

### STAFF ROLE

- Place the cones on the wing at each basket.
- Encourage quick rotations to save time.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

When is a good time to pass the ball to your teammate?

Load for younger players

MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-1 I MORE

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

Quickly introduce ROB shots (Range, Open, Balance). Divide players into groups of four with one ball per group. Two offensive players will position themselves either in the corner and wing beyond the 3PT line (on either side), or slot to slot beyond the 3PT line. One defender starts with a ball, a short closeout position away from the two offensive players. When the ball is passed in, the offense has a maximum of two passes to find an open shot, but they cannot move or dribble. The defender can attempt to steal the pass or block the shot. The offensive players look to shoot and score whenever they are open. The second defender waits on the side for the first 2-on-1 to complete before they rotate in. The defenders take turns playing defense for six repetitions. After six shots, the offense and defense switch roles. Three groups can go simultaneously at the same time on each basket.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, start the offense at the short corner and elbow (closer in) and use a smaller ball.
- The offensive players are allowed to drive at any time. However if an offensive player drives, only 1 pass is allowed.
- The offensive players are allowed to cut to the basket.
- The second defender starts in the paint and can defend after the initial pass, making it a 2-on-1+1.

### STAFF ROLE

- Help the players with their spacings and roles.
- Encourage defender(s) to find ways to disrupt the offense.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Was your shot a ROB Shot? If not, what was missing?
- In what ways can the defenders disrupt the offense?
- Is it possible to overpass?

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Identifying ROB shots (Range, Open, Balanced)
- Scoring off 2-on-1 advantages

MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

3-ON-3 RANDOM POSSESSION CHANGE

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Players will play continuous 3-on-3 in the half-court, playing until one team scores the ball. When this happens, the team that gets scored on sprints off, while the waiting team comes onto defense. On possession changes, players must clear the ball outside the 3PT line. If the coach yells ball, the player in possession of the ball must place it down, and sprint to hi-five the coach. The team on offense now becomes defense, while the team previously on defense becomes offense. Once the player has high-fived the coach, they can play defense again.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- If the offense does not score within six seconds of receiving the ball, it is an automatic turnover.
- Players have a dribble limit of three dribbles every catch.

### STAFF ROLE

- Yell out BALL in a random manner, approximately once every 15 - 40 seconds.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- How can you space effectively to use the advantage on the possession change?
- Defensively, how can you communicate to ensure you cover the ball and basket when in a disadvantaged situation?

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Spacing and advantage

MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

4-ON-4 CHANGING RIMS

20 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available full-courts

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per court

### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of four, based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get a point. The losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on defense at the opposite end. The team that gets a point gets to maintain possession and stay on offense. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The changing rims load: when the offense crosses the half-court line, they can change the basket in which they are attacking at any time. The entire team must cross the half-court line to change direction.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure quick changes after one team secures the win and a new team sprints on-court.
- Explain the changing rims load.

### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Spacing and advantage
- Passing and ball movement
- Transitioning back on defense and stopping the ball

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- When is a good time to pass in a 2-on-1?
- How can you space the floor effectively?

MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-2+1 CLOSEOUTS

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

### DESCRIPTION

In groups of four or five, the offense will start in any location in the mid-range or behind the 3PT line. The defenders will stand in any location within a reasonable passing distance to the offense, positioned at any distance between two to four meters away from the offensive players (approximately four to eight big steps). As soon as the ball leaves the passer hands, the defense can begin to closeout. The offense has two dribbles per catch to score. After three repetitions in a row, the players will change roles.

### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Attacking closeouts without traveling
- Closing out on defense by running out quick and stopping naturally (no choppy steps)

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The defense can only use one hand to contest.
- The passer must dribble and send a one handed pass to the defender.
- The +1 can be used as a screener if the offense does not convert the advantage off the closeout start.

### STAFF ROLE

- Make sure players start from different angles and locations.
- Ensure the defense stands four to eight steps away and closes out from different positions.
- Officiate the 2 dribble maximum load.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- What other location or angle have you not played from yet?
- Can you explore different ways to pass?

MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED

24 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

### DESCRIPTION

Divide the players into teams of five players, based on the number of courts available. Try to have a maximum of five teams on each full-court. In instances of very high numbers, half-courts can be used. Teams play to three baskets. After a team scores three baskets, they get 1 point. The losing team will rotate off while the next team waiting rotates on. The game is then continually played, with teams keeping track of their total number of points over the course of the activity.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Inside the 3PT line is lava. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the 3PT line unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the 3PT line).
- Pass and cut is a turnover: create an advantage through static 1-on-1.
- Double teams that lead to turnovers result in an extra 3 points.
- No ball pressure results in the defensive team losing 1 point and the offense regaining possession on the sideline.

### SCORING

3 baskets = 1 point for team.

### KEY WORDS

- How can you get the most efficient shot?
- How can we help teammates to emphasize continuous ball pressure?
- What can you do to space the floor effectively?

### STAFF ROLE

- Organize the waiting teams on the sideline so teams transition quickly for the next repetition.
- Ensure players substitute every few minutes.
- Emphasize and teach offensive and defensive concepts and philosophy.
